summary: Lina Wang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. She studied at Peking University and held a post at the National Library of China.
Lincoln T. Zacconi works in philosophy and indology. He completed a specialization at Faculdade da Aldeia de Carapicuíba in 2016 and pursued a master's degree at the University of São Paulo in 2017.

Linda Hogan is a religious studies scholar educated at Maynooth University, St Patrick's Pontifical University, and Trinity College Dublin (PhD, 1991). She held posts at Chester, Leeds, and Trinity College Dublin, where she served as Vice-Provost (2011–2016).
Linda Jean LaMacchia specializes in indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2001) under doctoral supervisor David M. Knipe.
Linda Learman is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. Her studies include doctoral work supervised by Robert P. Weller and postdoctoral mentorship under Peter N. Gregory (both attested 2005).
Linda Penkower is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who earned her PhD from Columbia University in 1993. She was a research fellow at Taisho University (attested 1983).
Linda York Leach (1942–2006) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and indology. She studied at the University of Michigan and completed her PhD at Case Western Reserve University in 1978.
Lindsay G. McCune is a scholar in tibetology and religious studies. She completed an MA under Bryan J. Cuevas and studied under Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan.
Lindy Li Mark is an anthropologist and sinologist who held posts as professor of anthropology at California State University, East Bay, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Ling Ji is a sinologist who completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore (attested 2014) under the supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo.

Linnart Mäll (1938–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, tibetology, and indology. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1957–1962) and under Bidia Dandaron (~1966–1972), later holding a post at Tartu from ~1969 to 2010.
Linus Klemp is a scholar in Buddhist studies, tibetology, and indology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (attested 2026 as a PhD Fellow) and held a PhD post there in 2025.
Lionel Burton Burrows (1883–1970) was a scholar in linguistics and indology. He was educated at St. Paul's School, Darjeeling, and Elphinstone College.

Lionel David Barnett (1871–1960) was an indologist and linguist who studied under Edward Byles Cowell at Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum (1899–1936, 1948), University College London (1906–1917), and SOAS (1917–1948).
Lionel James Trotter (1827–1912) was an indologist, historian, and archaeologist who was educated at Charterhouse School and Merton College.

Lionel Obadia is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Lille in 1997. He held positions at INALCO, KU Leuven, EPHE, Lille 3 University, and Lumière University Lyon 2.

Liqian Liu (1910–2008) was a scholar in tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at West China Union University (~1946–1949), the translation administration department of the State Council, and Ethnic Publishing House.

Lisa Grumbach is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and japanology. She has held posts at Stanford University (attested 1996) and as an assistant professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Lisa N. Owen specializes in indology, history, and archaeology. She earned her MA and PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Janice Leoshko, and also studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995.

Lise Menn is a linguist who studied at Swarthmore College, Brandeis University, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She held an academic post at the University of Colorado Boulder from 1986 to 2007.
